notable_absence.predicate: hasCardinality / requiresExactly (no such predicate exists in the registry)
notable_absence.finding: The page never states in words that an analyzer has exactly one tokenizer and zero-or-more character/token filters - that cardinality is only implied by the UI shape (step 8 says 'click the tokenizer you want to use', singular selection from a list with no add/remove affordance, versus steps 7 and 9's explicit 'To add ... / To remove ...' list operations for character and token filters). I modeled all three as hasInternalComponent without a cardinality qualifier, since the registry has no predicate or datatype property for 'exactly one' vs 'zero or more' sub-components - the same subsumption-vocabulary gap noted in earlier rounds (indexes.md's notable_absence) shows up here as a cardinality gap instead.

cross_component_finding: This page is the assembly point for the four 'create-custom-*' analyzer-component pages in this batch (create-custom-character-filter.md, create-custom-tokenizer.md, create-custom-token-filter.md, and create-custom-wordlist.md via search:custom-analyzer-components' broader Word Lists category) - they are not four disconnected topics but one composed object's parts, exactly as the dispatch brief suspected. The procedure's own step order and verbs state the composition and its direction explicitly: character filters act 'before tokenizing' (pre-tokenization), the tokenizer 'create[s] tokens from Search input', and token filters 'modify the tokens created by the tokenizer' (post-tokenization) - so the three component families are not just co-located UI sections but a stated processing pipeline (character filters -> tokenizer -> token filters), which hasInternalComponent captures the containment half of but not the ordering half. There is no promoted or extraction-layer predicate in the registry for pipeline/processing order (e.g. a 'precedes'/'appliesBefore' shape) - only hasInternalComponent (containment) and requiresPriorExecutionOf (statement-ordering, not applicable to a per-request text-processing pipeline) exist, so the ordering fact is stated in this record's evidence quotes but not captured as a separate relation.
cross_product_finding: No measured Capella twin for this page (create-custom-analyzer.md is not among the eight filename-identical pairs this round's dispatch flagged), so no cross_product_finding fires per the evidence-gate rule against forcing a comparison with no real content on both sides. The nearest Capella-side content is cloud/search/customize-index.json's search:custom-analyzer-components and search:analyzers, both minted from a single UI-gating sentence ('You cannot create custom analyzers or custom filters if Advanced Options are not enabled') rather than from a procedure - Capella's own dedicated custom-analyzer creation page, if one exists on disk, has not been read in this round.
